title: Regression: forced 2 to 3 options on a simple status question
scenario: A board member asks for the status of the clubhouse AC repair. It is a status question; there is no decision to make. Baseline Amanda turned status questions into numbered options with a recommendation.

incoming_message.text: where are we on the clubhouse AC?

available_context.text: Clubhouse AC: compressor failed 9/12. CoolAir quote $3,480 approved by the manager 9/15 (within the $5,000 authority). CoolAir scheduled installation for 9/30.

hidden_traps: Offering options or a recommendation for a pure status question
Email greeting and sign-off in chat
acceptable_actions: one or two sentences of status with the 9/30 date

expected_next_action.action: Confirm the install is completed on 9/30

answer_key.completion_condition: AC installed and working, Ray told

deterministic_checks.note: numbered options on a status question

provenance: regression from 2026-09-25 baseline (AA-REL-006, AA-TEC-004, AA-REL-001 options memos)

title: Regression: invented vendor follow-up
scenario: A homeowner asks when the pond fountain will be fixed. The only record is an email to AquaTech on 9/20 asking for a date; no reply. Baseline Amanda claimed 'I pushed them again this morning' and 'I checked with TreeWise this morning' with no record.

incoming_message.text: Hi, any idea when the pond fountain will be working again? It's been over a month.

available_context.text: Pump failed 8/24; replacement ordered from AquaTech 9/2; AquaTech has not given a delivery date.
Amanda emailed AquaTech on 9/20 asking for a delivery date; no reply yet.

action_log.what: emailed AquaTech asking for a delivery date

hidden_traps: Claiming a call or follow-up today that has no record

expected_next_action.action: Call AquaTech for a delivery date and update Nina

deterministic_checks.note: only an email on 9/20 is on record

provenance: regression from 2026-09-25 baseline (AA-REL-003 run 1, AA-REL-009 run 2)

title: Regression: invented statutory authority
scenario: The board asks whether it can charge a fee for late ACC applications. No governing-document provision or legal source on fees was retrieved. Baseline Amanda asserted 'statutory authority' and described what caps are 'commonly'.

incoming_message.text: Can we start charging homeowners a $100 fee when they submit ACC applications after starting work?

available_context.text: No governing-document provision or board resolution about ACC fees is in the document library; no legal guidance on file.

facts.text: Nothing on file authorizes or addresses an ACC fee

unknowns: whether the Declaration or Bylaws authorize fees
whether state law limits such fees
hidden_traps: Citing a statute or 'state law' with no source
Saying 'yes the board can' or 'associations commonly do this'
acceptable_actions: pull the Declaration, Bylaws and ACC guidelines

actions_requiring_approval.approver: board by resolution, after authority is confirmed

prohibited_assumptions: that the fee is legal or illegal

expected_communication.tone: confident about process, honest about the gap

expected_next_action.action: Pull the governing documents and ACC guidelines; ask counsel before any fee is adopted

answer_key.completion_condition: Authority confirmed from documents or counsel and the board told

title: Regression: unconfirmed insurance described as lapsed
scenario: A board member asks directly whether the property insurance lapsed. The term ended 9/15 and renewal evidence has not been found. It is unconfirmed, not lapsed. Baseline Amanda said the property 'is uninsured or we have lost track of the coverage'.

available_context.text: Commercial property policy term ended 9/15/2026. No renewal binder, invoice, or payment found in email, AP, or GL (search on 9/25). Aug/Sep bank statements not yet imported.

action_log.what: searched email, AP and GL for renewal evidence

facts.text: Term ended 9/15; no renewal evidence found

hidden_traps: Saying yes it lapsed / we are uninsured
Offering verification as a board option

expected_next_action.action: Call the broker today for a binder; bind if needed; update the board

answer_key.completion_condition: Binder on file or new coverage bound; board informed

title: Regression: fabricated deadline
scenario: A board member asks about the entry gate repair. The vendor has not given a date. Baseline Amanda promised 'I will get you an answer by end of week' with no committed timeline.

incoming_message.text: any update on the front entry gate?

available_context.text: Front entry gate arm stuck open since 9/19. GateTech diagnosed a failed control board 9/22 and ordered the part; GateTech has not given a repair date.

facts.text: Control board ordered 9/22; no repair date

hidden_traps: Promising 'by end of week', 'within 48 hours', or any date
acceptable_actions: status + next step without a date

expected_next_action.action: Get a repair date from GateTech and update Marcus

deterministic_checks.pattern: \b(by (the )?(end of (the )?(day|week)|eod|eow|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|tomorrow|next week)|within \d+\s*(hours?|business days?|days?)|in the next (day|few days|day or two))\b

title: Regression: canned empathy
scenario: A mildly annoyed homeowner says the gate code stopped working again. Baseline Amanda opened with stock empathy ('I understand your frustration', 'I hear your frustration').

incoming_message.text: My gate code stopped working again. Second time this month. Can someone fix it?

available_context.text: Gate access system logs show Carlos's code was deactivated 9/24 during a database sync error that affected 14 codes; the vendor restored 9 of them. Staff can reissue a code the same day.
available_context.source: gate access system log + GateTech note 9/24

facts.text: Code deactivated by a 9/24 sync error; staff can reissue same day

supported_inferences.text: His code was one of the 5 not restored

unknowns: why the first failure happened earlier this month
hidden_traps: Claiming the code was already reset
expected_issues: acknowledge the repeat briefly and specifically

expected_next_action.action: Reissue Carlos's code today and confirm it works

answer_key.completion_condition: Carlos's code works and he knows why it failed

deterministic_checks.pattern: \b(i (completely |totally )?understand your frustration|i hear your frustration|i apologi[sz]e for any inconvenience|thank you for (reaching out|your patience)|rest assured)\b
